With Lake Jocassee at maximum drawdown, Bad Creek station in the pumping mode, the upper reservoir at maximum drawdown, and a minimum inflow from the Whitewater River, the tailwater would be lowered approximately 0.5 feet and have a maximum velocity of 5.6 feet per second in the intake structure openings.
To protect the public from the hazards of high velocities and turbulence around or near the Bad Creek outlet structure on Lake Jocassee, audible and visual warning signs would be placed along both sides of the discharge cove downstream of the discharge structures.
1.4.3 Access Roads and Tunnels
A permanent paved access road approximately 4 miles long would extend from South Carolina State Highway Route 171 around the north side of the proposed upper reservoir to the powerhouse access tunnels. Temporary roads would be required for use during dam construction and related work. The permanent access road would be routed to avoid major streamflows and to minimize silting during construction (Figure 1-1).
From the terminus of the permanent access road, a tunnel 29 feet high, 34 feet wide, and 1,400 feet long would provide access to the underground powerhouse (Figures 1-3, 1-4, and 1-5).
1.4.4 Transmission Facilities
A vertical shaft would be constructed to house the electrical bus and an elevator, and to provide ventilation. It would be about 800 feet high and 28 feet in diameter.
